series: JLPT N3 grammar exercise series (local work items N3-01 to N3-17)
status: content-complete; model-reviewed; production JVM importer verified; release-gate-open
scopeStatement: No official JLPT grammar list exists. Coverage is defined against the three official grammar item types and a frozen denominator of 220 Bunpro N3 entries, cross-checked against JLPT Sensei N3 and the Shin Kanzen Master N3 grammar syllabus. Levels are editorial estimates; nothing here is a claim of exam readiness.

sources.primary: Bunpro N3 (220 entries), per docs/jlpt-levels.md source precedence
sources.tertiary: Shin Kanzen Master N3 grammar (about 54 lessons), used as an independent completeness check
sources.unavailable: Tanos was unreachable during planning and is not used
sources.official: jlpt.jp item-type descriptions and the 2018 N3 sample (★-position composition, multi-blank passages)

rules.A: An item Bunpro lists at another level keeps that level; Sensei/SKM disagreements are recorded in the owning set ledger.
rules.B: An item Bunpro does not list is authored at N3 only when both Sensei and SKM place it at N3; one source only means deferred.
rules.C: Where the exact exercise sense fits N2 and N3 placement cannot be verified reliably, the task is labelled N2 and excluded from N3 counts.
ruleCList: ないわけにはいかない
rules.ruleCNote: The Rule C items keep their existing N2 labels and stay outside the N3 baseline and counts; no new exercise needed an N2 label.
notSeparateEntries: てばかりいる: the て-form sense of Bunpro N3 ばかり (nothing but), practised in its top-up

deferredCandidates.reason: One source only (Rule B); not authored.

officialItemTypes.proxies: Sentence composition orders full chunk sequences instead of the official ★-position choice; text grammar models a multi-blank passage as several one-blank exercises on the same passage. Both are functional proxies, not equivalents.

levels.policy: Each task is labelled by the most advanced grammar in its complete visible contrast; lower labels are allowed only with the reason recorded in the owning set ledger.

C1.criterion: Each of the 220 Bunpro N3 entries has a disposition with a reason

C2.criterion: Sensei- and SKM-only topics adjudicated under the source rules
C2.result: pass: 〜通す added under Rule B; one-source topics deferred (see deferredCandidates)

C3.criterion: Every relationship side exercised; formation, interpretation and transfer separated
C3.result: pass by n3check per set (each facet at least two distinct context keys) and three blind reviews per set

C4.criterion: The three official grammar item types each have exercises

C5.criterion: Text-grammar passages respect the short/mid/long register without reproducing reading comprehension
C5.result: pass by N3-16 review: 46 passage exercises, 128-197 characters, one tested slot per exercise and no candidate printed outside its blank

C6.criterion: Grammar and the substantive contrast are classified, not vocabulary or kanji
C6.result: pass by the level audit and per-set level reasons

Native Android ContentSync/Room run on a device: not performed. The production JVM importer and a Robolectric run of the real ContentSync, WebP verification and Room code passed against the pinned archive (local HTTP fake); see acceptanceRecord.
Public sync: not performed; the branch is local and unpushed. A complete immutable local ZIP with SHA-256 and exact budgets is recorded in acceptanceRecord; it is not a public release.
App work item V1-V5 (n3-grammar-plan/app-work-item-n3-grammar.md): partial JVM/static evidence only; physical-phone checks remain open.
limits: Levels are editorial estimates under Bunpro precedence; JLPT publishes no grammar list.
Typed mode hides options, so every instruction names its candidates; choice mode shows an additional correct label in about 20% of appearances.
Composition and text-grammar items are proxies for the official formats (see officialItemTypes).
